title: Week 19 Mastery Quiz · International Relations Theories

questions.question: A realist analysis treats security competition as central; a liberal-institutionalist analysis examines cooperation through agreements. What makes the comparison rigorous?
options: Specify predictions and evidence that could distinguish the explanations
Assume the theories predict exactly the same conduct
Select evidence supporting only realism
Treat theoretical terms as historical events
questions.explanation: Specify predictions and evidence that could distinguish the explanations

questions.question: A treaty is signed but implementation is uncertain. Which institutionalist question is most relevant?
options: The location of the signing photo
What monitoring, information, dispute resolution, and compliance mechanisms exist
Whether all signatories share a language
Whether the treaty uses long clauses
questions.explanation: What monitoring, information, dispute resolution, and compliance mechanisms exist

questions.question: A constructivist study examines how a state's stated identity changes across decades. Which evidence would help?
options: Military budgets alone
One unexplained speech
Dated official discourse, policy practice, audience, and rival interpretations
The state's flag colors
questions.explanation: Dated official discourse, policy practice, audience, and rival interpretations

questions.question: A postcolonial critique questions why a policy history starts only at formal independence. What is the methodological issue?
options: Independent states have no earlier history
Any timeline is equally explanatory
Colonial legacies are always the single cause
Periodization may omit institutions and power structures shaped earlier
questions.explanation: Periodization may omit institutions and power structures shaped earlier

questions.question: A feminist IR approach investigates whether security policy affects populations differently. Which evidence is appropriate?
options: Disaggregated impacts, participation, institutional choices, and lived risks
Only the number of national leaders
A single national average treated as universal
Only a statement by an official spokesperson
questions.explanation: Disaggregated impacts, participation, institutional choices, and lived risks

questions.question: A dependency perspective claims trade patterns reinforce structural inequalities. What would most directly test it?
options: A map without economic data
Longitudinal trade, value-chain control, bargaining capacity, and alternative mechanisms
A speech using the term dependency
Only the number of signed trade agreements
questions.explanation: Longitudinal trade, value-chain control, bargaining capacity, and alternative mechanisms

questions.question: The UN Charter Articles 1–2 address security and peaceful settlement. What distinction should a student draw?
options: The Charter predicts every state's decision
All IR theories are codified in the Charter
The Charter states legal principles; competing theories seek to explain observed behavior
The Charter eliminates power asymmetry
questions.explanation: The Charter states legal principles; competing theories seek to explain observed behavior

questions.question: A country joins a coalition after a crisis; analysts offer balance-of-power and shared-identity explanations. What study could distinguish them?
options: Choose the more familiar label
Use only the date of the announcement
Assume coalitions cannot have multiple motivations
Compare decision records, threat assessments, identity narratives, and contrary cases
questions.explanation: Compare decision records, threat assessments, identity narratives, and contrary cases

questions.question: A study equates economic interdependence with guaranteed peace. What qualification is necessary?
options: Interdependence can change incentives but its effects depend on institutions, distribution and strategic conditions
Trade totals prove all disputes resolved
Any trade agreement removes security dilemmas
Trade and conflict cannot be studied together
questions.explanation: Interdependence can change incentives but its effects depend on institutions, distribution and strategic conditions

questions.question: Two theories explain the same outcome after the fact. Which design strengthens the test?
options: Use vague predictions
Identify contrasting observable implications in advance and inspect disconfirming evidence
Exclude outcomes neither theory predicted
Measure the theories by popularity
questions.explanation: Identify contrasting observable implications in advance and inspect disconfirming evidence

shortResponse: How do competing theories explain state behavior, institutions, identity, conflict, and cooperation?
rubric: 10 points: precise claim (2), accurate concepts (2), two specific pieces of evidence (2), reasoning (2), counterargument or limitation (1), revision condition (1).
